title: hydo project (format 1)
description:
A hydo project, format 1: what runs in the guest, the workload, the properties, the faults that
make sense, and the test composer's plan. Experimental until hydo 1.0; within format 1 keys are
only added. String values may contain {{param}} references (params:).

format.description: The project format: 1. A document without format: is read as format 1.

hydo_version.description: The hydo the project was made for (checked against hydo's own version).

name.description: The project's name: lowercase letters, digits and '-'.

network.description:
loopback (default): one network for everything; bridge: each service in its own network
namespace at its addr:.

root.description: What goes on the read-only root filesystem.

data.description: The read-write data disk, mounted on /data: the fault target.

shell.description: Shell helpers, sourced before every command.

params.description:
Build parameters: {{name}} in any string value is replaced by the default here or by
`hydo build --set name=value`.

configs.description:
Build parameters whose values `hydo explore --configs` explores (Milestone 299): one image
per combination of values, each explored with the same seeds, and a table of the failures
found with each value. Each key is a parameter of params:; its default comes first.

services.description: The long-running processes, started in dependency order.

groups.description:
Named sets of services (the nodes of a cluster) that fault tokens aim at as a whole:
K=<group>.majority@..., P=<group>.primary@..., N=<group>.halves@... (MANIFEST.md
"Groups of services").

provision.description: Run once after every service is ready, before the snapshot every schedule starts from.

workload.description: The workload in numbered steps (with test commands: only steps and timeout).

knobs.description: Durability settings the explorer may relax.

invariants.description: Properties as shell commands, run by the init.

checks.description: Ready-made checkers of recorded histories, run on the host.

faults.description: The fault kinds that make sense for this project (default: all but freeze and protocol).

freeze_match.description: Payload strings that mark the packets a freeze sweep tries first.

fakes.description: Fake outside services, served and recorded in the guest.

proxies.description: Fault proxies in front of real services.

emulators.description:
Ready-made emulators of outside services (Milestone 242, docs/design/emulators.md): one
entry runs a pinned emulator (a Docker/OCI image, fetched by `hydo build`) as a service,
with a fault proxy of the same name in front of it, so that `H=` faults and the record
work as for a fake. Its service keeps the explorer's other faults off.

browser.description:
A web application tested through its own Playwright tests (Milestone 253,
docs/design/web-apps.md): the tests run unchanged in a pinned Playwright image (fetched by
`hydo build`) as the workload, and hydo watches the pages for uncaught errors, spinners
that stay, failed requests that the page never shows, and texts such as NaN. Needs
`network: bridge`; it writes the workload.

errors.description: Error logs as findings: true, or a mapping.

buggify.description: The programs carry BUGGIFY fault points (the schedule token B= sets them).

steer.description:
Numbers the system's output reports that say how close a run came to failing: `hydo
explore --steer <id>` keeps the schedules that came closest and changes them a little
(docs/design/steered-search.md).

clock_points.description:
Times a clock fault may step the guest's clock to, in the schedule language's form
(`@HH:MM[:SS]`, `@:MM[:SS]`, `@hour`, `@day`, `@month`, `@year`, each with an optional
offset such as `+10m` or `-2s`; UTC): `hydo explore` draws `T=<at>:<point>` among its
clock steps, so a time of day or a calendar boundary that the system acts on is reached
(MANIFEST.md "Clock steps to a time").

perf.description:
Measure the workload's work for performance tests (Milestone 237): each run's
`result.json` gets `perf`, and `hydo perf compare` compares two runs. On hvx the count is
the guest's retired branches, exact and the same in every run of one image; on KVM and the
Mac it is VM exits, which do not count CPU work.

contracts.description:
Function contracts (Milestone 241): programs of `root.files` whose sources carry
`// hydo: requires ...` and `// hydo: ensures ...` comments next to functions. `hydo
build` compiles them with each program's debug information into `<image>.contracts.json`,
and the engine checks them at every call (docs/design/contracts.md; MANIFEST.md
"Function contracts").

test.description: The test composer's plan (the hydo/ folder fills it too).

VersionPin.description: The hydo the project was made for: "0.3" (that release or a newer one of the same major; an older hydo refuses), "0.3.1", or ">=0.3" (at least that release, of any major).

Scalar.description: A string, a number or true/false.

ram_mib.description: Guest RAM in MiB: 256..8192 (every engine; the host needs that much free per running guest).

clock_start.description: Unix seconds the realtime clock starts at.

clock_after_cut.description: After a power cut the recovery boot's clock continues from the cut plus this many seconds.

outcomes_after_cut.description:
After a power cut the recovery boot's $HYDO_OUTCOMES starts with the first boot's last
outcome of every id (without it the file starts empty there). On by default for images
built at fingerprint epoch 6 and later; an image built earlier keeps it off (the schema's
default is that of the released format). false: the file starts empty there.

cpu_cache.description:
x86_64: the guest's CPUID describes a fixed cache hierarchy (32 KiB L1 data and
instruction caches, a 256 KiB L2, an 8 MiB L3), the same on every host and engine. On by
default for images built at fingerprint epoch 2 and later; an image built earlier keeps it
off. false: the cache leaves are empty, and at cpu v3 the glibc 2.28 of Red Hat Enterprise
Linux 8 and its rebuilds (AlmaLinux 8, Rocky Linux 8, UBI 8) crashes in memcpy.

kernel.description:
A guest kernel variant. containers: on the Mac and KVM engines the image boots a kernel
with what containers and Kubernetes need (namespaces, seccomp, the memory and pids
controllers, overlayfs, connection tracking, NAT, iptables, nftables, ipsets), all built
in. hvx boots its one kernel, which has all of it, the network parts as modules that the
image loads itself. Without the key, the engine's usual kernel.

root.description:
Where the Mac engine's image keeps its root file system. memory: the whole root is the
initramfs, in guest RAM (the default without browser:). disk: a read-only ext4 file system
on the image's disk, which a small initramfs mounts (the default with browser:), so a root
of gigabytes fits. The x86_64 engines always boot the root from the disk.

reboot.description:
A guest program may ask for a reboot with the console line HYDO-REBOOT: hydo shuts the
guest down cleanly, starts a new boot of the same machine with the disks' bytes, and goes
on with the next workload step (docs/design/devices.md).

disks.description:
Disks beside the main disk, each with a write cache of its own: /dev/vdb, /dev/vdc, ...
in this order, empty at the first boot (the Mac and KVM engines; docs/design/devices.md).

branch_tick.description:
The KVM engine interrupts guest code that runs without a VM exit after a count of its
user-mode conditional branches, a point the guest alone fixes, so a loop that waits for
another thread gives way (an Intel host with a counter of the guest's branches; the Mac
engine refuses the image; docs/design/exit-free-loops.md).

cgroup2.description:
hydo mounts the cgroup2 file system on /sys/fs/cgroup at the start of every boot, as a
container runtime does, so a program that reads /proc/self/cgroup at start finds its
cgroup. On by default for images built at fingerprint epoch 4 and later; an image built
earlier keeps it off. false: the guest starts without the mount.

exact_tick.description:
The hvx engine boots the guest kernel with its TSC as the clock (`tsc=reliable`, and a
virtual TSC that moves 1 us per step), so the guest's clocks follow the virtual TSC
exactly, read in steps of 2 us. Without it the guest kernel keeps time with
refined-jiffies, which counts a tick as 999,848 ns while its timer is set 1 ms apart: the
gap grows by 152 ns a tick, and a guest that keeps its CPU busy late in a long run finds
its clock nearly stopped. On by default for x86_64 images built at fingerprint epoch 5 and
later; an image built earlier keeps it off. The Mac and KVM engines ignore the key
(Milestones 319 and 323; MANIFEST.md, "The guest's timer tick on hvx").

path.description:
Every command that hydo starts in the guest (the workload's, the checks', a service's
own) gets PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin in its
environment, so a program that such a command starts finds the guest's programs, hydo-oci
among them, by name. Without it the commands have no PATH: busybox's shell finds the
programs, but Go's exec.Command("hydo-oci") does not. Off by default for images built at
fingerprint epoch 5 and earlier, because the variable is in guest RAM and so in every
fingerprint (Milestone 348); on for images built at epoch 6 and later.

proc_io.description:
The Mac and KVM engines boot the guest with a kernel that has per-process I/O
accounting, so the guest has /proc/<pid>/io, which some programs read at start (brpc in
Typesense stops without it). The default for images built at fingerprint epoch 7 and
later; an image built earlier keeps the kernels it was built for. false: the guest
kernels of epoch 6, without the file, and their timing. hvx's guest kernel always has the
file (Milestone 376).

ParamRef.description: A string with a {{param}} reference, replaced by params: before the value is checked.

RootPlace.description: Where an arm64 image keeps its root file system (Milestone 284).

name.description: A letter, then letters, digits and -, at most 16 bytes.

cache.description:
volatile: writes wait in the disk's cache until a flush of that disk, and a power cut
loses them; none: every write is durable at once.

DiskCache.description: The write cache of an added disk.

Network.description: How the services reach each other.

size_mib.description: Default: 1.3 x the content, rounded up to 64 MiB.

nix.description: Nix store paths; each full closure is copied to the same path.

files.description: Host files or directories copied into the guest.

text.description: Small files written inline: guest path -> content.

share_images.description:
Image services with the same image (by config digest) share one unpacked tree; each still
has its own mount of it, with its own /tmp, /data, volumes and tmpfs mounts. Off by
default (it changes the image's bytes).

fix_pyc.description:
Timestamp-checked Python bytecode caches (__pycache__/*.pyc) get the image's fixed file
time and their source's size in their header, so Python uses them instead of compiling
the sources again in every run. On by default (images built at fingerprint epoch 2 and
later); false leaves the caches as the image has them.

Text.description: A string, or a whole number (written as its digits).

src.description: Relative to the manifest, or ~ / absolute.

ConfigSetting.description: A build parameter that `hydo explore --configs` explores (Milestone 299).

values.description:
The values to explore, each once. The parameter's default (params:) comes first, listed
here or not.

service.description:
The service whose configuration the parameter is (a name of services:), or a list of
them (the nodes of a cluster that share one configuration file).

doc.description: Where the project documents the setting (a link or a file).

tradeoff.description:
The values whose documentation says they weaken a promise, each with that note. A failure
found only with such values is reported as the setting's documented trade-off, not as a
bug.

ServiceNames.description: One service's name, or a list of them.

name.description: [a-z][a-z0-9_]*: also the name fault tokens use (K=<name>@...).

cmd.description: Runs in the foreground (an image service: replaces the image's Cmd; a list = argv).

setup.description: Run before every start (also restarts and crash recovery).

ready.description:
Exit 0 = ready; polled once per second. `tcp:<port>` (or `tcp:<host>:<port>`): ready when
a connect to the port succeeds; the host defaults to `addr:`, else 127.0.0.1.

port.description: The port network faults act on.

addr.description: The service's own address (loopback 127.x.y.z, or 10.89.x.y with network: bridge).

recovery.description: false: not started for the power-cut recovery check.

restart.description:
What hydo does when the service's process ends by itself while the test runs, in Docker
Compose's words: no (the default: it stays down until the heal), always, unless-stopped,
on-failure, on-failure:<max>. Followed by agent images (MANIFEST.md "Restart policies").

restart_may_fail.description:
true: the restart at the heal (after the faults, before workload.retry) may fail. If the
service does not come back then, the run goes on without workload.retry; a power cut at
the k-th flush (cf=) still reaches its recovery boot, which gives the verdict; without a
cut the verdict is ERROR naming the service. Default false: a service that does not come
back is at once ERROR (MANIFEST.md "A restart after the faults that may fail").

job.description:
true: a one-shot job, such as a database migration, that other services run in their
setup: before they start (`hydo compose` writes it for Docker Compose's
service_completed_successfully). Its own process only idles, so hydo explore never draws
a fault on it (MANIFEST.md "One-shot jobs").

start_after.description:
When hydo starts this service: ready (the default) waits until every service before it in
the start order passed its readiness check; started waits only until each of them was
started, so a cluster whose readiness check needs its peers can start (Docker Compose's
depends_on condition service_started). Every service is ready before provisioning and the
workload either way (MANIFEST.md "Starting services together").

logs.description:
More log files the service writes besides its output (absolute paths; shell patterns such
as /data/db/log/*.log are allowed). The diagnosis of a failed run and `hydo inspect logs`
show their last lines too.

compare.description:
A command that prints the state the service stored, for comparisons of two versions of
the system (`hydo compare-versions`; Milestone 298): for example a SQL query or a scan of
every key. After the verdict, in the boot that gives it, hydo runs it and reports each line
of its output as `HYDO-STATE <service>: <line>`, at most 64 KiB (MANIFEST.md "State for
comparisons").

clock.description:
`own`: the service gets a wall clock of its own (Milestone 372). It starts under
`/bin/hydo-clock`, and `T=<svc>@<at>:<change>` steps its clock (`T=n2@5:-30`,
`T=n2@5:1500ms`) or makes it drift (`T=n2@0:200ppm`), while the other services and the
checks keep the guest's clock (MANIFEST.md "One service's own clock"). x86_64 images
only.

errors.description: This service's error-log settings (needs the top-level errors:).

image.description: A Docker/OCI image file the service's files come from.

image_ref.description: Which image in the file: a tag or sha256:<digest>.

entrypoint.description: Replaces the image's Entrypoint (and drops its Cmd).

env.description: Added to or overriding the image's Env.

env_file.description:
A file of KEY=VALUE lines, relative to hydo.yaml, read when the image is built: its
values are added to the image's Env before `env:`, which wins. It keeps values such as
passwords out of hydo.yaml: `hydo k8s` writes one per service for its Secrets, in a
folder that version control ignores (MANIFEST.md "Values from a file").

mounts.description: Bind, volume and tmpfs mounts of an image service.

writable.description:
true: the image service's root is writable, as a container's: a copy of the image on the
data disk (its layer), kept when the service is killed and restarted, and after a power
cut as far as it was flushed (MANIFEST.md "A writable root for image services").

storage.description:
Where the service keeps its data, for the faults that hit one service's storage
(MANIFEST.md "Storage faults of one service"): a directory under /data (G= corrupts files
there), or {dir:, size_mib:} to make that directory the service's own file system on the
data disk (L=, a power loss of this service alone).

version.description:
The name of the version that cmd:, setup: and ready: run (needed with versions:). An
upgrade token (U=<name>@<at>:<version>) switches the service to another version and back
(MANIFEST.md "Versions of a service and upgrades").

versions.description:
The other versions of the service an upgrade token can switch it to, each with the
commands that differ from the service's own. Every command of the service sees the name
of the version it runs as $HYDO_VERSION.

CommandLine.description: An argv list (exec'd, no shell), or a shell command string.

RestartPolicy.description: Docker Compose's restart: words: no (the default), always, unless-stopped, on-failure or on-failure:<max> (0 = no limit); false (a bare YAML no) means no.

StartAfter.description: When a service starts: once every service before it is ready, or once each has started.

ServiceClock.description:
Whose wall clock a service reads (Milestone 372): `own` starts it under hydo-clock, so that
`T=<svc>@<at>:<change>` steps it or makes it drift while the other services keep the
guest's clock.

files.description: More log files the service writes (absolute paths).

normalize.description: More parts to blank out of the template.

ErrorFormat.description: How a service's log is read.

ErrorLevel.description: Which log lines are error lines.

Normalize.description: A regular expression (replaced by *), or {pattern, replace}.

ImageSource.description: A Docker/OCI image: a `docker save` tar or an OCI layout directory, or one per architecture.

src.description: A guest path (bind or volume); or give tmpfs: true.

copy_up.description: Copy the image's files into src on first use (a volume).

Storage.description: A service's storage: the directory under /data, or the directory with its own file system.

dir.description: The directory, relative to /data (or starting with /data/).

size_mib.description:
The size of the service's own file system (a partition of the data disk, ext4 with a
journal, mounted on the directory), 16 to 3072 MiB. Without it the directory stays on the
shared data file system.

ServiceVersion.description: Another version of a service (`services[].versions`, Milestone 238).

name.description:
The version's name, as U= writes it: a letter or digit, then letters, digits, '.', '_'
and '-' (3.6.0, 3.6.0-rc.2, v2).

cmd.description: The command this version runs (default: the service's cmd:).

setup.description: Run before every start of this version (default: the service's setup:).

ready.description: This version's readiness check (default: the service's ready:).

Group.description: A group of services that fault tokens select from.

services.description: The members, services of this manifest, each once. Selectors count them in this order.

primary.description:
A command that prints the service name of the group's current primary (leader) on its
first line and exits 0; run in the guest when a fault aims at <name>.primary.

restart.description:
How the members come back after a fault killed two or more of them (Milestone 374):
one-by-one (each after the one before is ready), or together (all started, then each
one's readiness checked), for a cluster whose members get ready only with a quorum.

links.description:
Which links between the members the explorer may cut with `network: bridge` (Milestone
374): depends_on (only those that name each other there, the default) or all (every two
members, for a cluster whose nodes talk to each other).

GroupRestart.description: How a group's killed members are started again.

GroupLinks.description: Which links between a group's members the explorer draws network faults on.

kind.description:
`system` (the default): the workload drives a system through numbered steps, and faults
are placed at steps. `test` (added in M205): the workload runs a test program (a unit or
integration test, often once, in step 0); the explorer then takes one step, draws no
service faults unless `faults:` lists them, and classes a failure as `test-failed`.

steps.description: Faults are placed at step numbers (1..1000; with test commands: rounds, default 20).

run.description: Runs steps [HYDO_FROM, HYDO_TO); not with test commands.

retry.description: Runs after the faults heal (no power cut).

process.description: A pgrep -f pattern telling whether a request is in flight (default: run's first word).

WorkloadKind.description: What a workload is: a system under a stream of requests, or a test program (M205).

token.description: One capital letter, not a built-in schedule token.

default.description: The value the image starts with (the safe one).

cmd.description: Exit 0 = holds, 1 = violated, 2 = could not be evaluated now.

every.description: Also check every this many seconds of guest time during the workload.

final.description: Check at the end (default: true unless every: is given).

within.description: type: eventually: the deadline in seconds of guest time.

after.description: type: eventually: the anchor of the deadline.

InvariantType.description: What kind of property an invariant is.

Anchor.description: Where an eventually property's deadline counts from.

HistoryCheck.description: A history check: the workload records operations (hydo_hist), the host checks them.

history.description: The history the workload records under.

final.description:
A shell command that reads the final state back into the history (type: messages: the
drain, which reads every message at the end and records `drained <channel> <group>`).

include.description:
type: messages: bundles of declarations (YAML files of the project, relative to the
manifest), merged in order, then this entry's own keys; hydo build resolves them.

acknowledgement.description: type: messages: how consumers acknowledge deliveries.

retention_ms.description:
type: messages: a message may legitimately disappear this many milliseconds after it was
sent (an excuse for a missing message, not a claim).

clock_steps.description: type: messages: whether time-dependent claims judge pairs across a T= clock step.

claims.description: type: messages: what the system promises; every default claims nothing.

measures.description: type: messages: what the measures cover.

HistoryModel.description: The object a linearizable history is checked against.

HistoryInitial.description: What a key holds before the first write.

Consistency.description: The consistency level a list-append history is checked against.

MsgAcknowledgement.description: type: messages: how consumers acknowledge deliveries.

MsgClockSteps.description:
type: messages: whether time-dependent claims judge pairs whose interval contains a T=
clock step (undecided: they are counted, never judged).

MessageClaims.description:
type: messages: the claims (docs/design/messaging.md). Each claim is checked and reported on
its own, as `<check id>.<claim>`.

acked_outcome.description:
Every acknowledged send ends in the final state that the check's `final:` reads back
(`status` records): succeeded, or failed with an error the client causes.

MsgDelivery.description: type: messages: what delivery the system claims.

MsgDuplicatesClaim.description: allowed, forbidden, or a deduplication window.

MsgDuplicates.description: type: messages: whether a message may be stored twice.

MsgDedupWindow.description: Sends with one id within the window are stored once (window_ms: 0 means always).

MsgDedupBy.description: type: messages: what a deduplication window compares.

MsgAfterAck.description: type: messages: whether an acknowledged message may come again.

MsgProcessing.description: type: messages: whether a message may be processed (acknowledged and accepted) twice.

ms.description: Milliseconds, or per-delivery (each delivery records its lease as v=).

MsgPerDelivery.description: type: messages: the lease each delivery records (v=).

MsgOrderClaim.description: An order kind, or a mapping with kind:, scope: and batch:.

MsgOrderKind.description: type: messages: the order the system claims.

MsgOrderScope.description: type: messages: the scope of an order claim.

MsgBatch.description: type: messages: whether the items of one send are in order.

MsgDeadLetterClaim.description:
none, or after how many deliveries without an acknowledgement a message stops (and where it
goes).

MsgDelayClaim.description: none, per-message (each send records its delay as d=), or one delay for every message.

MsgDelay.description: type: messages: when a message may be delivered.

MsgFanOut.description: type: messages: whether every group that must receive a message receives it.

MsgMembers.description: type: messages: whether two members of a group may hold one message at once.

MsgLinearizable.description: type: messages: the queue the sends and receives are linearizable as.

MsgAckedOutcomeClaim.description: none, success, or a mapping with client_errors: and effect:.

MsgAckedOutcome.description: type: messages: whether every acknowledged send ends as acknowledged.

client_errors.description:
The errors (`e=` of a status item) that the client causes, each a code or a pattern with
`*`: a failed final state with one of them keeps the claim.

effect.description:
recorded: the read-back records whether each operation's effect is there (`f=1` or
`f=0`), and a final state that contradicts it breaks the claim.

MsgEffect.description: type: messages: whether the read-back records each operation's effect.

MessageMeasures.description: type: messages: what the measures cover.

windows.description: Also per window of the run.

quantiles.description:
The quantiles of every distribution, from 0 to 1 (hydo's YAML reads 0.5 as the text
"0.5", which is taken as the number).

MsgQuantile.description: A quantile: a number from 0 to 1, or its text.

MsgChannels.description: all, or a list of channels.

FaultKind.description: A fault kind the explorer may use.

FreezeMatch.description: Payload strings for the freeze sweep: a list, or replies:/requests: lists.

Fake.description: A fake outside service (HTTP, or cleartext HTTP/2 gRPC).

idempotency.description: Where a request's idempotency key is (an extractor such as header:Idempotency-Key).

ref.description: Where a request's reference is (an extractor such as json:order).

tls.description:
HTTPS: the fake also answers TLS for these host names, with a certificate of the image's
own test CA, which the guest and every image service trust.

status.description: The HTTP status of the answer.

code.description: The gRPC status code of the answer.

message.description: gRPC: the answer message's protobuf bytes in hex.

effect.description: The route has an effect in the outside world (a charge, an email).

idempotent.description: The same idempotency key again gets the first answer and no new effect.

save.description:
Store fields of the object a request creates or changes, when it takes effect; later
answers read them as `{obj:<field>}`.

load.description:
The key (a template) of the object a request is about; a missing one is answered 404 and
takes no effect. The answer reads its fields as `{obj:<field>}`.

errors.description:
The answer bodies of an `H=` rule `status=<code>` on this route (templates), by status
(`'404'`), class (`'5XX'`) or `default`; without one, hydo's own error body.

if_header.description:
The route takes only a request that has this header, whatever its value (Milestone
329): `If-None-Match` or `If-Match` makes a route of an S3 client's conditional writes.
A request without it goes on to the next route.

WebhookSign.description: `sign:` of a webhook: an HMAC-SHA256 signature header on every delivery attempt.

header.description: The header that carries the signature.

secret.description: The endpoint secret; its bytes are the HMAC key.

payload.description: What is signed: `{ts}` (the attempt's Unix seconds), `{body}` and the webhook's values.

value.description: The header's value; `{hmac}` is the signature.

FakeSave.description: `save:` of a fake's route: the object's key and the fields to store (templates).

Tls.description: HTTPS for a fake or a proxy (MANIFEST.md "HTTPS for fakes and proxies").

hosts.description: The host names the system calls (e.g. api.stripe.com); /etc/hosts sends them here.

port.description: The TLS port on the endpoint's address.

Proxy.description: A fault proxy in front of a real service.

to.description: <address>:<port> of the real service (or give service:).

service.description: The service (with a port:) the proxy stands in front of.

tls.description: HTTPS: the proxy also answers TLS for these host names (and forwards in plain text).

idempotent.description:
http proxies (Milestone 242): a repeat of an idempotency key that took effect gets the
service's first answer and does not reach the service, as a provider that keeps
idempotency keys answers; needs the proxy's idempotency:.

errors.description:
http proxies (Milestone 329): the answer bodies of an `H=` rule `status=<code>` on this
route (templates), by status (`'412'`), class (`'5XX'`) or `default`; without one,
hydo's own error body.

if_header.description:
The route takes only a request that has this header, whatever its value (Milestone
329): `If-None-Match` or `If-Match` makes a route of an S3 client's conditional writes.
A request without it goes on to the next route.

Emulator.description: A ready-made emulator of an outside service (Milestone 242): `use:` names the catalog entry.

use.description:
The catalog entry: stripe (stripe-mock behind HTTPS for api.stripe.com), smtp (Mailpit),
s3 (rclone's S3 server).

name.description:
[a-z][a-z0-9_]*: the proxy's name, which H= tokens and the record's checks use (default:
the use: value). The emulator's service is <name>_emulator.

port.description:
The port the system calls (the proxy's plain listener; default: stripe 12111, smtp 1025,
s3 9000).

ref.description:
Where a request's business reference is (an extractor such as form:metadata[order]),
for the record and its checks.

tls.description:
stripe: HTTPS for api.stripe.com with the image's test CA (default true); false leaves
only the plain port.

buckets.description: s3: buckets that exist from the start.

durable.description:
s3: true makes every write that the emulator acknowledged survive a power cut of the guest
(Milestone 354; default false). The data folder and its buckets get ext4's attribute S
(chattr +S), so each write and each change of a folder reaches the disk before rclone
answers.

addr.description:
The emulator's service's address (Milestone 316). With network: bridge the default is
the first free one of 10.89.1.1, 10.89.1.2, ...

EmulatorKind.description: The catalog entry of an emulator.

Browser.description:
The `browser:` section (Milestone 253): a team's Playwright project, run unchanged as the
workload, and what hydo watches in its pages.

tests.description:
The folder of the Playwright project, relative to the manifest: its playwright.config,
its tests and its node_modules (run `npm ci` there first: the guest has no network). It is
copied to /opt/hydo/web/tests. Required unless `explore` is given.

explore.description:
A walk through the pages that hydo makes itself, instead of tests (Milestone 258): the
workload is a seeded walk, named by the schedule token I=.

playwright.description:
The version of @playwright/test in the tests' node_modules; hydo pins the Playwright
image of that version (default and only pinned version: 1.65.1).

name.description: The browser's service name (default browser); the invariants are <name>.<property>.

addr.description: The browser's address on the bridge (default 10.89.0.250).

shards.description:
Workload steps (default 1): step i runs shard i+1 of `playwright test --shard`, so that
faults can be placed between test files.

args.description: More arguments for `playwright test`, such as --project=chromium or --grep.

env.description:
Variables for the tests and the web server their config starts (the base URL of the API,
the folder of the built app).

must_pass.description:
Every test must pass (default true). Under faults the tests' own assertions often fail by
design; false keeps only the watched properties.

watch.description: What hydo watches in every page.

screens.description:
Which pages get a screenshot (default failures: a page that ends its test with a busy or
error element; all: every page at the end of its test; compare: all, and each compared
with the file of the same name in `screens_ref`, pixel for pixel, as the invariant
<name>.screens_match). The screenshots go to the run directory's screens/.

screens_ref.description:
The folder of the reference screenshots for `screens: compare`, relative to the manifest
(default hydo-screens): a passing run's screens/*.png. It is copied to
/opt/hydo/web/screens-ref.

read_back.description:
Milestone 334, with `explore` only: the check <name>.acked_shown, that the pages show
every object whose id the server acknowledged in a write. true takes the defaults: every
object that a POST or PUT returned an id of, on the walk's start page, as a link whose
path ends with /<kind>/<id> (the kind is the last word of the write's path). It runs at
the end of the run and in the recovery boot after a power cut.

BrowserExplore.description:
`browser.explore` (Milestone 258): hydo walks through the app's pages itself. Each workload
step is one part of the walk, in a fresh browser that keeps the cookies and the page of the
part before; each action is drawn from the schedule's I= seed and the page's accessibility
tree.

start.description:
The URL the walk starts on, as the browser in the guest reaches the app
(http://<a service's address or localhost>:<port>/<path>).

server.description:
A command line that starts the app's web server in the browser's service before each
step, as Playwright's webServer does (default none: a service serves the app).

steps.description: Workload steps (default 4, at least 4): a fault can fall between two parts of the walk.

actions.description: Actions in each step (default 10); I=<seed>,n<k> takes k.

setup.description:
Steps before the walk, such as signing in: each one of open, click (with role), fill
(with with), press, see, wait. They run in the first step without a saved session.

avoid.description: Regular expressions of control names the walk never uses (default: log out, sign out).

within.description: The walk follows only links under this path prefix (default /).

values.description: More texts the walk types into text fields, besides hydo's own edge values.

settle_ms.description: The wait after each action, in milliseconds (default 700).

quiet_ms.description:
The wait at the end of each step, before the browser closes, in milliseconds (default
3000).

BrowserSetupStep.description: One step of `browser.explore.setup`: one of open, click, fill, press, see or wait.

click.description: Click the button or link of this accessible name.

role.description: The ARIA role of the control that click names (default: a button or a link).

fill.description: Fill the field of this label or placeholder.

press.description: Press this key, such as Enter.

see.description: Wait until this text is on the page.

BrowserWatch.description:
What hydo watches in the pages of `browser:` (Milestone 253). An empty list turns its
invariant off.

errors.description: Uncaught exceptions and unhandled promise rejections are findings (default true).

console.description: console.error calls count as errors too (default true).

busy.description:
CSS selectors of busy elements: spinners, progress bars (default [aria-busy=true] and
[role=progressbar]).

busy_max_ms.description: How long a busy element may stay, in milliseconds (default 10000).

alerts.description:
CSS selectors of error elements: toasts, chips, banners (default [role=alert] and
[role=alertdialog]).

failures_within_ms.description:
How soon after a failed request an error element must show, unless the page sends the
request again, in milliseconds (default 5000).

requests.description: Only the pages' fetch and XHR requests under this path prefix are judged (default all).

failures_of.description:
A regular expression over a request's path: only a failed request that matches must be
shown (default every judged request), for example the writes of an API whose reads run in
the background (Milestone 258). It also matches `<METHOD> <path>`, such as
`^(POST|PATCH|DELETE) /api/` for an API whose reads and writes share a path
(Milestone 273).

text.description: Texts no page may print (default NaN, undefined, [object Object], Invalid Date).

answers.description:
The requests whose answers a page must show up to date (Milestone 393): true for every GET
request under `requests`, or a regular expression over a request's `<METHOD> <path>`. When
an answer comes after the answer of a newer request of the same method and path, the page
must show the newer one (the property `<browser>.newest_answer_shown`). Default off.

BrowserAnswers.description:
`browser.watch.answers` (Milestone 393): true, false, or a regular expression over a
request's `<METHOD> <path>`.

BrowserScreens.description:
Which pages of `browser:` get a screenshot (Milestone 254): those that end their test with
a busy or error element, every page at the end of its test, or every page compared with
its reference.

BrowserReadBack.description:
`browser.read_back` (Milestone 334): true, false, or which acknowledged objects the pages must
show, where and how.

objects.description: The kinds of objects to look for (default one entry of the defaults).

setup.description:
The steps that sign in when the check's browser has no session of the walk, as in the
recovery boot after a power cut (default the walk's own setup).

wait_ms.description: How long a page may take to show its objects, in milliseconds (default 10000).

BrowserReadBackObject.description:
One kind of object of `browser.read_back.objects`. {id} in page, shows and unless is the id
that the write's answer returned, and {<group>} a named group of writes.

writes.description:
A regular expression over `<METHOD> <path>` of an acknowledged write whose answer
returned an id (default `^(POST|PUT) `), such as
`^POST /api/projects/(?<project>\d+)/tasks$`.

name.description:
The object's name in the check's sentences, such as task (default the last word of the
write's path, in the singular).

page.description:
The path of the page that lists such an object, such as /orders/{id} (default the walk's
start page).

shows.description:
A Playwright selector of what shows the object on that page, such as
`a[href$="/tasks/{id}"]` or `text=Order {id}` (default a link whose path ends with
/<kind>/<id>).

unless.description:
A regular expression over `<METHOD> <path>` of a later acknowledged write that removes
the object on purpose (default `^DELETE <any path>/<kind>/{id}$`).

ErrorsSetting.description: Error logs as findings: true (every default), false (off), or a mapping.

max.description: The most error kinds one boot prints, 1..200.

services.description: The services whose logs are scanned (default: every service).

SteerValue.description:
A number in the guest's console lines that says how close a run came to failing (Milestone
209): the steered search's value.

match.description:
A regular expression (Rust's regex syntax) over each console line; its first capture
group (the whole match without a group) is the number. A run's value is the best match
of all its lines.

goal.description: min: a smaller number is closer to failing; max: a larger one.

SteerGoal.description: Which way a steered value is closer to failing.

steps.description:
Run each workload step as its own workload call and measure it (`step 3`), besides the
whole workload. Without it the workload runs in one call, as without `perf:`.

threshold.description:
The change in percent that `hydo perf compare` reports as a change; a smaller one reads
as no change (hydo's YAML reads 0.5 as the text "0.5", which is taken as the number).

PerfThreshold.description: A percentage from 0 to 100, or its text.

program.description:
The program's path in the guest: a `dst` of `root.files`, whose `src` is the program
with its debug information.

sources.description:
The folders (or files) of the program's sources, relative to the manifest: every `.rs`,
`.go`, `.c`, `.h`, `.cc` and `.cpp` file in them is read for `// hydo:` comments.

error_paths.description:
Watch the program's error paths (Milestone 306, docs/design/error-paths.md): the bodies
of Go's `if err != nil`, Rust's `Err` returns and arms, `?`, `unwrap()` and panics, and
functions named for a retry, a recovery or a rollback. Each run records which of them
ran; `// hydo: error path` and `// hydo: no error path` lines add and remove places. The
Mac engine watches them.

Test.description:
The test composer's plan: small commands composed into seeded rounds (the schedule token W=),
properties, and saved regressions. The hydo/ folder fills commands, checks and regressions.

parallel.description: At most this many commands at once (1..16).

round_ms.description: A round every this many ms of guest time (10..60000).

drain_timeout.description: After the last round, running commands get this long (1..3600).

budget_ms.description: 0 = none; else no command starts later than this after round 0.

first_records.description:
true: what the first commands write to $HYDO_ACKED and $HYDO_OUTCOMES during
provisioning stays in those files for the run, so operations made in the seed are among
the client's records (default false: the run's files start empty).

TestCommand.description: A composed command; its id is <kind>_<name>.

content.description: 8 to 64 lowercase hex digits: a hash of the command's code (an SDK computes it).

TestCheck.description: A composed check; its name is its property id.

every.description: kind always: seconds between checks (default test.check_every).

history.description: Retired (a history check written here; top-level checks: is its home).

TestCheckKind.description:
When a composed check runs. linearizable, list_append and list-append are retired here
(they are history checks: top-level `checks:`); format 1 still reads them, and `hydo
migrate` moves them.

TestRegression.description: A saved schedule replayed by `hydo repro --regressions`.

expect.description: ok (default), violation, or fp=<16 hex digits>.

commands.description: The command ids at save time (seed-form W= regressions written before M98).

compose.description: The resolved composition a W=@<key> names.

contents.description: Command id -> content hash at save time.

$comment: Generated from hydo-manifest's model (hydo/crates/hydo-manifest/src/model.rs); do not edit. Project format 1, experimental until hydo 1.0: within format 1 keys are only added. HYDO_BLESS=1 cargo test -p hydo-manifest --test format rewrites it.
